dataValue: Broadly, the foreign investment framework is designed to ensure that the proposed investment is not considered contrary to Australia’s national interest, including its national security interests. Foreign investments in that meet defined control (ownership) and monetary thresholds are assessed to ensure they are not contrary to Australia’s national interest.    Foreign investments that meet defined control (ownership) and monetary thresholds are assessed to ensure they are not contrary to Australia’s national interest, including national security.  This includes acquisition of sufficient interest in Australian land, an Australian entity, or an Australian agribusiness above the relevant monetary threshold. Foreign government investors require approval before starting a business in Australia.   Foreign investments that relate to Australia’s national security, regardless of monetary value, are assessed to ensure they are not contrary to Australia’s national security. This includes acquisition of sufficient interest in a national security business or national security land, or starting a national security business. National security businesses include telecommunications carriers and carriage service providers, and data storage and processing service providers.  The Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018 (SOCI) imposes notification obligations on owners and operators of critical telecommunications assets, including interest and control information. However, these obligations apply equally to foreign and domestic investors into critical infrastructure. SOCI defines data storage and processing service providers for the purposes of the FATA.  The Telstra Corporation Act 1991 (Telstra Act) limits foreign ownership of Telstra, telecommunications carrier that was formerly government-owned.
